title: Dot product

review.history: source gap; no origin or priority assertions

source_policy: Definition-level references support the mathematical vocabulary. All stories and worked quantities are original constructed teaching scenarios, not measurements or historical events. Historical priority and notation claims require separate claim-level evidence before publication.
purpose: Measure how real vectors align and follow the scalar into a signed projection.
meaning: The Euclidean dot product sums products of corresponding components and returns a scalar. For nonzero vectors it relates length and angle; projection needs a nonzero reference. General inner products can use other rules or complex conjugation.

signature.projection: signed scalar projection onto u; null for u=0
signature.projectionX,projectionY: components of the projection vector v onto u; null for u=0
signature.angleDegrees: angle when both vectors are nonzero; null otherwise

conditions: Use corresponding real Euclidean components in the same axis order.
The dot product is a scalar and may be positive, zero or negative.
Projection onto u needs nonzero u; an angle needs both vectors nonzero.
definition.domain_notes: Only the standard real dot product for four components in [-4,4] is executable. Zero vectors keep the dot product defined while auxiliary projections/angles can be null. Physical examples require compatible component/product units.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level reference; worked properties are author-derived for stated assumptions. Independent mathematical review pending.

grammar.pronunciation: Dot product in real two-dimensional coordinates
grammar.formation_rule: output=dot=ux*vx+uy*vy; uNorm=hypot(ux,uy); vNorm=hypot(vx,vy); projection=dot/uNorm and projectionFactor=dot/uNorm² when uNorm>0, otherwise null; projectionX=projectionFactor*ux; projectionY=projectionFactor*uy; both projection components are null when uNorm=0; angle requires both norms positive.
grammar.precedence: Multiply corresponding entries before adding or subtracting. Ordered coordinates and matrix entries retain their stated positions.
